text:
maya: Heads-up - seeing a surge of tiny-gpu pods stuck Pending in us-west1a starting ~09:12 UTC. Lots of latebinds failing attach/heartbeat, then scheduler marks as unschedulable and we get eviction churn.
jonah: Yep I noticed - looks like allocate path races with node heartbeat TTL. Pods bind then lose node shortly after. Any recent scheduler changes?
maya: No scheduler rollout AFAIK. We did push a kubelet hotfix last night (attach-detach timing tweak). Could be interaction.
liam: Can you paste a sample of the kube-scheduler logs and pod events?
maya: Paste of events from one pod: ```Warning FailedScheduling 09:12:34 pod/mini-job default 0/100 nodes are available: 100 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 50 node(s) had insufficient resources, 30 node(s) were not ready.``` Also attach-detach errors in kubelet: ```error "nvlink: attach timeout""```
anya: Hmm the mix of taints + warmnode churn + attach timeout smells like latebind picking cold racks. Are these tiny GPU pods with fractional-ish requests?
maya: Yes most are tiny 0.125/0.25 GPU jobs that prefer warmpools. Latebind should avoid cold nodes but timing's off.
jonah: Metric check: scheduler bind latency and kubelet heartbeat gap. I'm seeing scheduler.bind.duration spike to ~1.8s and node.heartbeat.miss_count up across the AZ at 09:11-09:14.
ops-oncall: We're ramping up a mitigation - temporarily increasing the kube-scheduler lease TTL and warmpool grace window. That should reduce false unschedulables while we investigate.
liam: Quick patch idea: change latebind to double-check node readiness after bind but before finalizing, maybe with a 500ms probe. Reduces race but adds latency.
anya: Also consider backoff on attach attempts to avoid thrashing NVLink/attach subsystem. If drivers are overloaded, retries just make it worse.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-031 - "latebind heartbeats -> pending + eviction churn". Linked alerts: node-heartbeat-gap (sev3), scheduler-bind-latency (sev3).
maya: I'm going to collect more traces: kube-scheduler logs around bind, kubelet attach logs, and the warmpool allocation timeline. I'll post aggregation in an hour.
jonah: Meanwhile roll out ops-oncall change and monitor token rolling gauge: warmpool.healthy_count and scheduler.bind.failure_rate. If that drops, we know it's the TTL race.
liam: If we see persistent attach timeouts, we should throttle tiny-gpu launches per rack and instruct warmpool allocator to prefer nodes with recent attach successes.
anya: Agreed. Long term: a soft affinity policy for warm nodes + prefer-local NVLink topology plus a small hold window post-bind.
\m aya: typo in prev message - will attach logs soon.
ops-oncall: Mitigation deployed at 09:23 UTC (increased scheduler lease TTL by 1s, extended warmpool hold by 2s). Watching metrics now.
maya: Update 09:28 UTC - Pending count dropped ~70%, eviction churn stopped. Still seeing a few attach timeouts on older racks.
jonah: Good sign. Next steps: 1) root cause trace + correlate with last night's kubelet push; 2) telemetry dashboard for latebind races; 3) backlog ticket to add post-bind readiness probe + backoff.
liam: I'll open the ticket and add a small canary for the probe change.
anya: I'll draft ops runbook: when pending spike with attach errors, extend TTL + check warmpool health, throttle new tiny-gpu launches to target racks.
maya: Thanks all. Posting logs in the thread now -> https://redwood-internal/links/INC-2026-031-logs (internal).
